args.root_cause:
Heap grew rapidly (about 385 MB to 684 MB of 768 MB within roughly 70 s) with no change in entities or players. This began right after StatsCache's config was changed at 07:18:38 and reloaded at 07:18:39 with retain-history=true and history-size=1000 (it had been retain-history=false at startup). The correlation is strong but I did not confirm it with a heap dump, and I don't know who made the config change. Separately, my own action caused a ~80 s outage: I sent 'reload confirm' over RCON to try to apply the config change in-process. Paper treated it as a plugin reload, disabled all plugins and the server went down at 07:19:57. It did not come back until I started it at 07:20:34.</root_cause>
<parameter name="actions">Checked status and logs; observed heap rising quickly (385 -> 684 MB) and an unexplained StatsCache config reload (retain-history=true) at 07:18:39. Declared incident. Read StatsCache stats.json (tiny) and config.yml. Wrote plugins/StatsCache/config.yml to retain-history: false, history-size: 1000. Sent 'reload confirm' via console/RCON to apply it; this caused a plugin-reload shutdown and the server went DOWN at 07:19:57 (my mistake). Started the server with server action 'start' at 07:20:34. Verified after restart: StatsCache logged retain-history=false, status UP, TPS 20, 2 players online, heap stable between roughly 318 and 406 MB over about 3 minutes, mspt about 1-4 ms. No players banned, no files deleted, no world data touched.</actions>
<parameter name="resolved">true
args.residual_risk: The root cause of the heap growth is inferred from timing, not proven. retain-history was set back to false, but history-size is still 1000 and the change that enabled history was not reviewed by its author. If someone re-enables retain-history, the leak may return. Players were disconnected for about 90 s (from 07:19:57 to 07:20:36) because of my 'reload confirm' command. The heap sawtooth looks like normal GC, but the baseline should be watched. Anyone who changed StatsCache config at 07:18:38 should be told about the change and the rollback.
